output.methodChoice: Collected 2 items: X7 (site-level counts with go-live and staffing status), then X3 (booking reconciliation from app audit logs and callbacks). Used the specified diagnostic sequence internally: compared sites with and without the app and with and without a coordinator, checked the mechanism and dose-response, and tested the renewal, satisfaction and competitor explanations against the same data.
output.brief:
Mara, the evidence doesn't support cancelling RotaWeave. The fall comes from two changes together, not either alone.

Millbrook (app, coordinator kept) went 118 to 111; Quarry Lane (coordinator lost, no app yet) 86 to 80; Dock Street and Westgate (both changes) roughly halved, 217 to 104. On the basic tier, a regular keeps a weekly slot only if staff book it before Thursday's release. At those two sites staff made about 74 such bookings a week until 30 April, then 3. Of 213 regulars there, 129 lost their usual slot; 88% of them are now inactive, versus 11% of those who kept it. Of 61 lapsed volunteers reached, 44 cited a lost shift and 2 joined another group; 121 of 123 lapsed had current background checks.

I'm fairly confident (about 85–90%). Unknown: how many lapsed volunteers will return.

Next: at Dock Street and Westgate, use the idle admin seat to pre-book regulars weekly, phone lapsed ones offering their slot back, and review after 60 days. Arrange the same cover before Quarry Lane goes live on 6 October. Don't cancel the contract, suspend background checks, or hide inactive names.
